transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Morgan (Redwood AE), Diego Patel (Redwood SE), Jamie Chen (SummitEdge - Channel Lead), Marcus Lee (SummitEdge - Solutions Architect), Priya Natarajan (SummitEdge - Head of Partnerships)

Summary / quick notes: Intro to reseller program, go-over of lead flows and commission/margin guardrails, technical pilot gating items, SOC2/KMS questions, agreement to run a joint pilot and follow up with technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. Uh, quick intro round, I'm Alice, AE on the Strategic Partners team at Redwood, and with me is Diego, our sales engineer.
[00:12] Jamie Chen: Hi Alice, thanks — Jamie here, lead for channel at SummitEdge. We've got Marcus and Priya on the line as well.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Marcus, solutions. Good to meet you both.
[00:21] Priya Natarajan: Priya. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:25] Alice Morgan: Cool. Agenda — we'll walk through the reseller onboarding flow, lead routing, a couple of co-sell plays we've run, then technical gating for pilots, and finally pricing/margins and next steps. Anything to add?
[00:36] Jamie Chen: Sounds right. Also want to hear how you handle deal registration and protection — that's a big ask from our sellers.
[00:41] Alice Morgan: Totally. We'll cover that.
[00:44] Diego Patel: Quick note — when we talk infra later I'll outline the VPC/private options and how the runtime handles prefix caching and KV cache — sorry, K-V cache — sometimes transcription types that sound odd.
[00:55] Marcus Lee: Perfect. We need to confirm SSO and KMS flows too.
[00:58] 
[01:02] Alice Morgan: Ok starting with the playbook — we've done a few low-touch resellers and a few strategic ones. For SummitEdge we recommend a hybrid approach: enablement + lead sharing + joint credits for first two pilots. High-level steps: NDA/co-sell agreement, enablement workshops, pilot, then scaled handoff to Redwood's account teams.
[01:27] Jamie Chen: How long is your enablement? Our sellers want quick ramp, 2–3 hours ideally.
[01:32] Alice Morgan: We do a 90-minute enablement for sellers — product overview, pricing rules, and how to register deals in our portal. Deeper technical stuff is a separate 90-minute technical deep dive.
[01:42] Priya Natarajan: That seems reasonable. Pricing — what's the typical margin for resellers?
[01:46] Alice Morgan: We typically keep a band: advertised list price, then a reseller margin we honor via partner discounts — usually 15–25% depending on commitment and joint marketing. For strategic launches we can do higher co-funded credits. We'll put exact brackets in the playbook.
[02:01] Jamie Chen: And deal registration protection?
[02:04] Diego Patel: Deal reg is portal-based — you submit the account, we validate minimal criteria (customer open RFP stage or pilot agreement), and then we lock the opportunity for 90 days. There's a low-friction process.
[02:18] Jamie Chen: Good. Any restrictions on using hosted vs dedicated for pilot customer data?
[02:23] Alice Morgan: We support hosted for most pilots; if customer requires data residency or VPC-only we can spin up Redwood Private options — that's an enterprise conversation. For pilots we often run hosted unless there's a hard requirement.
[02:36] Marcus Lee: On technical side — what are minimum infra requirements? We need to map to customer environments.
[02:40] Diego Patel: For a standard pilot we need a small VM to host integration pieces and network access to our endpoint. If it's a dedicated or private deployment, you'll need VPC peering and KMS integration for encryption at rest. Also, token caching behavior — prefix caching — can be configured. Note: sometimes transcripts say KV cache, but implementation details change per model.
[03:03] Priya Natarajan: SOC2 — many of our customers ask. Do you have SOC2 Type II and audit logs we can present?
[03:09] Alice Morgan: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and our security pack includes audit log exports. We'll share the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report under NDA.
[03:18] Jamie Chen: Great. On enablement collateral, can we co-brand a one-pager and a short demo recording? Our sellers like short videos.
[03:25] Alice Morgan: Yes, we'll provide a co-branded one-pager and a 10–12 minute demo clip.
[03:31] 
[03:33] Alice Morgan: Now touching on technical validation: we typically ask for two acceptance criteria for a pilot — 1) accuracy/quality thresholds on a holdout prompt set, and 2) latency under a SLO for typical request size. We can attach a template.
[03:47] Marcus Lee: For latency, our enterprise customers want sub-500ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
[03:52] Diego Patel: For hosted models with short prompts we often hit sub-300ms median depending on model and region. We can also route to dedicated capacity for consistent tail latency if needed. There's a cost tradeoff.
[04:05] Jamie Chen: Cost tradeoffs are important — how do you recommend we price to end customers? Do we use a margin on list or fixed per-seat?
[04:12] Alice Morgan: Most partners price per-usage with a markup; some offer subscription tiers for predictable billing. We'll include sample pricing calculators.
[04:20] 
[04:23] Priya Natarajan: Contract language — do you have standard reseller terms or does everything go via legal? We prefer short MSA addenda.
[04:30] Alice Morgan: We have a reseller addendum template that sits on top of our standard MSA. We can share that; legal review is expected for strategic deals but most can use the template.
[04:40] 
[04:43] Jamie Chen: On leads — can SummitEdge bring leads into your pipeline and still own upsell? How is attribution handled?
[04:49] Diego Patel: Lead attribution happens via registration and CRM tags. If you register the opp, you get primary attribution for first 12 months; renewals have configurable rules. We'll coordinate with your CRM integration.
[05:02] Marcus Lee: CRM integration — what connectors do you support?
[05:05] Alice Morgan: We integrate with Salesforce primarily; we can also accept CSV uploads for bulk registration.
[05:12] 
[05:15] Alice Morgan: Let's talk about a sample co-sell play we ran with another reseller — quick case: they registered a pilot with a fintech customer, Redwood provided $25k pilot credits, partner handled outreach and onboarding, final deal closed at 4x pilot spend. We find pilots convert if there's joint customer executive engagement.
[05:38] Jamie Chen: Good to hear. Appetite for joint marketing? We can commit to two webinars in quarter one if Redwood can co-sponsor and help with content.
[05:47] Alice Morgan: Yes, co-marketing is in scope. We can co-sponsor webinars and run joint case studies for successful pilots. Marketing ops will coordinate assets and demand gen tracking.
[05:57] 
[06:00] Diego Patel: Technical Q — Marcus, can you share typical dataset sizes and whether customers want embeddings or text-generation?
[06:06] Marcus Lee: Mostly text-generation for customer support workflows, occasionally embeddings for search. Datasets are small for pilots — 5k–20k records.
[06:14] Diego Patel: That maps well. For embeddings we have separate pricing units. For generation we monitor token usage; we'll demo the cost/latency tradeoffs in the deep dive.
[06:25] 
[06:27] Alice Morgan: Ok I'm going to call out the pilot acceptance doc — we'll send a template that includes success metrics, SLOs, data access, and approximate timeline (2–6 weeks typical).
[06:37] Priya Natarajan: Timeline is important — what does your enablement calendar look like?
[06:40] Alice Morgan: Enablement can be scheduled within a week of contract; technical deep dive within two weeks. Pilot length depends on scope, but standard 4 weeks recommended.
[06:50] 
[06:53] Jamie Chen: One sticky point — discounts for our sellers on renewals. We need clarity on ongoing margin.
[06:59] Alice Morgan: We can define renewal discount tiers in the reseller agreement: baseline 10% for renewals, escalators tied to volume. We'll document scenarios.
[07:10] 
[07:12] Marcus Lee: For private deployment options — is on-prem supported for pilot?
[07:17] Diego Patel: On-prem is heavier lift and usually reserved for enterprise customers. For pilots we recommend hosted or VPC. If a pilot absolutely requires on-prem we can discuss a limited private deployment proof but that adds lead time.
[07:29] 
[07:31] Jamie Chen: Any regulatory or data residency callouts for EU customers?
[07:36] Alice Morgan: We have EU regions and can route traffic to EU-only infra; also support regional KMS per customer. We'll share a data residency FAQ.
[07:46] 
[07:49] Priya Natarajan: Ok let's line up next steps — what will Redwood send?
[07:53] Alice Morgan: We'll send the onboarding deck, playbook PDF, reseller addendum template, SOC2 report (NDA), pricing calculator, and a demo clip. Diego will draft the technical deep dive agenda.
[08:06] Jamie Chen: We'll nominate two priority accounts and get Marcus to compile their environment details.
[08:12] Alice Morgan: Great. Anything else from SummitEdge?
[08:15] Marcus Lee: Not from me.
[08:17] Priya Natarajan: No, that's clear.
[08:19] 
[08:20] Alice Morgan: Alright we'll follow up by EOD Friday with the materials and propose times for the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[08:28] Jamie Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:30] Marcus Lee: Thanks.
[08:31] Priya Natarajan: Bye.

[52:00] Meeting end (approx).
